title: devx-snippet-oscillation-and-rollback-playbook-2027
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents a lightweight operational pattern for managing small documentation and code snippets (SDK examples, API examples, quickstart templates) when we detect "oscillation" — frequent small changes that cause flapping user behavior, increased support tickets, or downstream breakage. The goal is to reduce developer disruption, make rollbacks safe and auditable, and provide canonical fixes for commonly seen failures.

Scope: applies to markdown/snippet content published on Developer Docs (docs-site), snippet artifacts included in SDK repositories, and small support-provided fixes that are surfaced through the docs site. Not intended for full API contract changes or major SDK releases.

Audience
- Developer experience engineers
- Docs engineers and technical writers
- SDK maintainers and release engineers
- Support engineers who triage snippet-related incidents

Definitions
- Snippet: any short example of code/CLI/YAML embedded in docs or SDK README that is intended to be copy-pasted by users.
- Oscillation: repeated, rapid edits to the same snippet or doc page within a 7-day window that correlate with increased user incidents or revert commits.
- Canonical fix: a vetted code change or patch and an accompanying explanation that resolves a frequently observed failure mode.

Signals and detection
1) Telemetry signals to monitor
   - Page-level bounce: docs-site page view -> copy action -> support ticket opened within 24 hours. (tracked via docs telemetry)
   - Search for keywords in support tickets: "404", "example fails", "cannot import", "snippet error".
   - Git activity: >3 commits touching the same snippet file or page within a 7-day window.
   - SDK usage errors: crash reports referencing example stack frames or file names included in snippets.

2) Alerting threshold (example)
   - Trigger an internal alert when any of the following occurs within one week:
     a) 5 or more support tickets referencing the same snippet id or page
     b) 3+ commits reverting or patching the same snippet
     c) An automated test that validates snippet output fails on main for >=2 CI runs.

Roles and ownership
- Docs-ops (primary): triage, stage rollback PRs to docs staging, coordinate communication.
- SDK-maintainers (secondary): verify that snippet changes are consistent with SDK behavior and API contracts.
- Support (observer): provide ticket data and user repro steps.
- Release and CI team (executor): apply staged rollbacks to the live site and coordinate hotfix branches.

Playbook: triage and mitigation (step-by-step)
1) Triage (within 1 hour of alert)
   a) Assign a triage owner from docs-ops.
   b) Collect artifacts: page id/path, snippet id/anchor, last 7 commits touching snippet, related support ticket IDs, failing CI jobs.
   c) Run the snippet in a local environment (use the docs snippet runner or the SDK reproducibility harness).

2) Decide action (15–60 minutes)
   - If snippet is functionally incorrect and causes user-facing errors: prepare a rollback to the last known-good revision.
   - If the snippet requires a minor patch (typo, import path change) that can be validated quickly: create a hotfix PR, attach unit / example validation, and run staged check.
   - If the snippet reveals an API contract/behavior change: open an incident and escalate to SDK-maintainers and product.

3) Execute rollback or patch
   a) Rollback: open a docs staging PR reverting to last-good commit, add the "rollback-oscillation" label, link the support tickets, and request a 1-hour review.
   b) Patch: create a minimal PR with a clear changelog entry in the PR description and automated snippet runner checks.
   c) CI gating: require snippet-runner job and link to smoke test results.

4) Post-deploy validation (30 minutes after merge)
   - Validate the page in staging and production: execute the snippet in the canonical runner, confirm no regressions in other examples on the page.
   - Update the support tickets with the resolution and note the PR link.

5) Retrospective (within 5 business days)
   - Add notes to the related page's audit trail: cause, fix, review comments, and owner.
   - If the oscillation is recurring, schedule a design review to propose a longer-term change (snippet templating, stronger CI).

Canonical fixes catalogue (examples)
- Fix: Python import path changed after refactor
  - Symptom: "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood.client'" after copying snippet.
  - Canonical fix: update import to "from redwood import Client" and add module availability check to snippet runner.
  - PR checklist: unit test that imports module, example invocation output snapshot.

- Fix: CLI flag renamed between SDK minor versions
  - Symptom: "unrecognized arguments: --verbose-logging"
  - Canonical fix: update CLI example and add preferred flag comment with version note.

- Fix: Streaming response JSON envelope changed (new top-level key)
  - Symptom: examples parsing response.error when previously parsing response.data
  - Canonical fix: change example to use safe accessor pattern and document migration tip.

Snippet lifecycle and governance
- Naming convention: snippet IDs must be kebab-case and include a 3-letter area prefix (e.g., sdk-auth-refresh-01).
- Ownership: every snippet must have an owner alias in the frontmatter (author + team).
- Review cadence: high-use snippets (top 50 pages by copy rate) require quarterly review.
- Deprecation policy: mark snippet "deprecated" with an explicit date and link to replacement snippets.

Docs CI / snippet runner (config table)
| CI job | Purpose | Required artifacts | Failure action |
|--------|---------|--------------------|----------------|
| snippet-runner | Execute code examples in an isolated container | snippet id, language, image tag, fixture input | Block merge, create automatic revert PR template |
| docs-staging-deploy | Lint + preview site | built HTML, snippet ids | Block merge if rendering errors |
| smoke-examples | Run smoke tests against staged endpoints | post-preview snapshot | Post-deploy rollback alert if mismatch |

Example snippet-runner YAML (canonical)
```yaml
name: snippet-runner
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - name: Setup Python
    uses: actions/setup-python@v4
    with:
      python-version: '3.11'
  - name: Install snippet harness
    run: pip install -r tools/snippet-harness/requirements.txt
  - name: Run harness for snippet ${{ inputs.snippet_id }}
    run: snippets/harness/run.py --id ${{ inputs.snippet_id }} --timeout 120
```

Rollback PR template (required fields)
1) snippet_id
2) reason: revert / regression fix
3) last_good_commit
4) repro steps and supporting tickets
5) validation steps performed
6) owner sign-off (docs-ops)

Support troubleshooting cheatsheet (top issues and fast remediation)
- Symptom: copy-paste error (bad import path)
  - Fast remediation: add a small preface in the snippet showing the minimal virtualenv and pip install commands; link to an SDK quickstart.
- Symptom: example uses unstable internal API
  - Fast remediation: replace with stable wrapper example; flag internal behavior in notes and open SDK issue.
- Symptom: runtime version mismatch (Python 3.10 vs 3.11)
  - Fast remediation: add version comment and run harness across supported images.

Communication and customer-facing notes
- For P0 regressions affecting multiple customers, use the normal incident workflow and publish a short docs-site banner: "Temporary fix applied to examples on <page>. For details see <PR link>."
- For non-customer-facing oscillation (limited to docs repo): update the page changelog and the support ticket with the PR link and a short explanation.

Observability and KPIs
- Mean time to rollback (MTTRollback): target <= 2 hours for snippet oscillation alerts.
- Percentage of snippet fixes validated by snippet-runner: target >= 95%.
- Support tickets citing snippet failures per month: target decline of 50% after canonical fix.

Longer-term mitigations and proposals
- Snippet templating: create a small templating layer that references the canonical example in one place. This reduces duplication and oscillation surface.
- Version-aware snippet rendering: inject SDK minor/patch version guards into examples and annotate with compatibility.
- Automated diff alerts: nightly job that detects changed code examples and creates a review ticket if tests fail.

Templates and quickstarts included with this playbook
- rollback-pr-template.md (text)
- snippet-frontmatter-spec.md (text)
- snippet-runner-sample.yml (yaml)
- support-repro-checklist.md (text)

Appendix: quick reference commands
- Run local snippet harness:
  - python tools/snippet-harness/run.py --id sdk-auth-refresh-01 --container python:3.11
- Create rollback PR from CLI:
  - gh pr create --title "Rollback snippet sdk-auth-refresh-01 to <commit>" --body-file rollback-pr-template.md --label rollback-oscillation
- Search support tickets for snippet failures (example Splunk/Kusto query):
  - index=support sourcetype=incidents "snippet" OR "example fails" | stats count by page_id

Contact and escalation
- Primary oncall: docs-ops oncall rotation (docs-oncall@redwood.internal)
- Escalate to SDK-maintainers: sdk-maintainers@redwood.internal
